chunks: So restrain yourself, Abu al-Abbas, may Allah have mercy on you,

in whatever passes through your tongue and hand of good and evil! For we are partners in that, and be in accordance with my good opinion of you, and let my opinion of you not be proven wrong; and peace.

key_terms.أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ: Abu al-Abbas (a specific honorific/name used for the governor)
key_terms.جَرَى عَلَى لِسَانِكَ وَيَدِكَ: What passed through your tongue and hand (speech and action)
key_terms.رَحِمَكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on you

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam Ali give to his governor regarding speech and action?
ai.summary: In this letter to his governor in Basra, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) emphasizes the shared accountability of the ruler and the ruled, noting that the people are partners in the consequences of the governor's speech and actions. He urges Abu al-Hasan to uphold the high expectations placed upon him, ensuring that his conduct validates the Imam's trust and does not lead to disappointment. This reflects the Shia principle of mutual responsibility in governance, where the leader's justice directly impacts the community's spiritual and social well-being.

en.sayed-ali-raza: O’ Abu’l-‘Abbās, may Allāh have mercy on you, keep yourself restrained

in whatever you say or do, good or bad about your people, as we are both partners in this (responsibility). Prove yourself according to my good impressions about you, and do not prove my opinion (about you) wrong; and that is an end to the matter.
